items.title: Extending a derivation to a completion, to a localisation, and to a finite type extension after multiplying by a power
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma has two easy parts and one hard part: a derivation D of a ring extends canonically to the I-adic completion, extends uniquely to any localisation, and, for a finite type extension R inside R' with R_g isomorphic to R'_g for a nonzerodivisor g of R', some power g^N times D extends to R' (statement lines 11753-11765). The proof is a 28-line argument (proof lines 11768-11795). For (1) it uses the Leibniz rule to see that D maps I^n into I^{n-1}, which gives compatible maps on the quotients R/I^n and hence a limit derivation; the verification of the derivation axioms is explicitly omitted. For (2) it gives the standard formula D(r/s) = D(r)/s - rD(s)/s^2 and leaves the axiom check to the reader. The hard part (3) chooses generators x_i of R' over R, picks N with g^N x_i in R, extends g^{N+1}D first to R_g by (2), computes g^{N+1}D(x_i) by the Leibniz rule, shows the result lies in R' for every generator, and finishes by checking the formula on monomials, which is what turns a statement about generators into a statement about all of R'.
